summary: Abed Matini presents a practical, demo-driven session on building a framework-free hybrid RAG system that avoids the "multimodal tax" of cloud LLM APIs. He identifies two key problems: uploading raw documents to cloud chatbots consumes tokens before any question is asked, and combining too many tools creates management complexity in production. His solution is a local-first architecture using Docling to convert documents to Markdown locally, then chunking and embedding them into PostgreSQL before user interaction. The demonstration features an FAQ assistant chatbot for a sample HR employee handbook. The stack includes Python/FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, Ollama for local LLMs (CPU-only), and LangFuse for observability. Matini details multiple chunking strategies: heading-based (each heading becomes a Q&A pair for traceable references), paragraph-based, fixed 512-character with 64 overlap, and sentence-based. He demonstrates screenshot/email ingestion using OCR for temporary updates. He distinguishes direct RAG (fixed pipeline, better for compliance) from agent mode (extra tools, less control, slower). He uses the smallest Qwen 2.5 model (0.5B parameters, ~400MB), finding that vetting data before sending to a smaller model reduces hallucination. For retrieval, he advocates hybrid search combining BM25 keyword search with cosine-distance vector semantic search, fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The session covers LangFuse telemetry for tracking conversations, sessions, models, response times, and cost estimation. Guardrails—including intent rejects, term dictionaries, and LLM classifiers—stop prompt injection and out-of-scope queries (e.g., medical escalations) in Python code before reaching the LLM, enabling rigid testing. A consent widget requires users to accept terms before chatting. The architecture uses no paid frameworks: Docling for parsing, PostgreSQL for storage, Llama for chats, and LangFuse for telemetry. The entire codebase runs on GitHub Codespaces with one command.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Heading-based chunking creates traceable Q&A pairs per heading, outperforming raw PDF upload which produces meaningless untrackable chunks
Agents implemented as plain Python functions avoid LLM latency (20-30 seconds for multi-agent loops) and eliminate hallucination risk through testable deterministic code
Hybrid search combining BM25 keyword and vector semantic search is essential: keyword for exact matches (products, SKUs, medications), semantic for meaning-based retrieval
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges BM25 and vector results to produce top-ranked answers; retrieval count should be tuned by use case
Direct RAG offers a fixed pipeline suited for compliance; agent mode adds tools but is slower and less controllable
Guardrails—intent rejects, term dictionaries, and LLM classifiers—must stop prompt injection and out-of-scope queries in Python code before the LLM, enabling rigid testing and predictable blocking
Vetting data before sending to a smaller LLM model reduces hallucination; smaller models like Qwen 2.5 0.5B safely say 'I don't have that information' instead of fabricating answers
Code-based prompting of do's and don'ts replaces long system prompts, making guardrails testable and deterministic rather than relying on LLM compliance
LangFuse provides local telemetry tracking conversations, sessions, models, response times, and estimated costs for external models
Only two models are needed: a small chat model and a small embedding model, runnable on Docker with one click

sections.title: Introduction and Problem Statement
sections.summary: Matini introduces himself and outlines two problems: uploading documents to cloud LLMs wastes tokens before questions are asked, and managing too many combined tools complicates production chatbots. He previews a three-section talk covering document ingestion, search/retrieval, and observability.

sections.title: Technology Stack and End-to-End Blueprint
sections.summary: Describes the stack: Python, FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, Ollama (local LLMs, CPU-only), and LangFuse. Outlines the pipeline: documents are converted to Markdown via Docling, chunked, embedded, stored in PostgreSQL, then retrieved and passed through the LLM with LangFuse observability.

sections.title: Optimizing Data Ingest and Chunking Strategies
sections.summary: Demonstrates local document ingestion avoiding cloud token costs. Contrasts raw PDF upload (producing meaningless chunks like 'signature date') with heading-based chunking where each heading becomes a Q&A pair. Shows the FAQ admin page, chunking demo, and chat with traceable references confirming which chunk generated each answer.

sections.title: Advanced Chunking Strategies and Screenshot Ingestion
sections.summary: Covers additional chunking approaches: paragraph-based (each paragraph becomes a chunk regardless of headings), fixed 512-character with 64-character overlap (32 from each side, best for unorganized data), and sentence-based. Demonstrates screenshot/email ingestion via OCR-to-text-to-Markdown for temporary updates like maintenance schedules, enabling quick drag-and-drop without manual cleanup.

sections.title: Python-Function Agents and Local LLM Selection
sections.summary: Explains agents as plain Python functions rather than LLM-based agents, prioritizing speed (avoiding 20-30 second multi-agent loops) and deterministic control. Shows toggleable agent settings for current date retrieval and product info. Uses smallest Qwen 2.5 model (0.5B parameters, ~400MB). Emphasizes passing only needed clear information to LLM to reduce hallucination.

sections.title: Hybrid Search: BM25 Keyword and Vector Semantic Retrieval with RRF
sections.summary: Details hybrid search combining BM25 keyword search (for exact matches like product names, SKUs, medications) with cosine-distance vector semantic search (for meaning similarity). Explains Reciprocal Rank Fusion to merge both result sets. Stresses tuning retrieval count by use case—products need more results surfaced, medical scenarios need fewer—and warns that too many results confuse users.

sections.title: Telemetry, Guardrails, and Model Selection
sections.summary: Covers direct RAG (fixed pipeline, good for compliance) vs. agent mode (extra tools, less control, slower). Demonstrates LangFuse telemetry tracking conversation IDs, models used, chunk counts, response times, and cost estimation for external models. Explains code-based guardrails using intent rejects, term dictionaries, and LLM classifiers to stop prompt injection and out-of-scope queries (e.g., medical escalations) before the LLM, enabling rigid testing. Notes system prompts are kept small because do's and don'ts live in code. Shows a consent widget requiring users to accept terms before chatting. Explains moving from a 7B to 0.5B model for speed, finding that vetted data with smaller models reduces hallucination. Concludes that only two models are needed (small chat model + small embedding model), and the architecture uses no paid frameworks—Docling, PostgreSQL, Llama, and LangFuse.
